not_this_letter_if: the letter is from Companies House (use companies-house-late-filing)
the letter is about paying Corporation Tax late (interest, not this rule)

penalties.applies_to: returns with a filing date on or after 1 April 2026

fixed.text: Return 3 months late: another £200 (£400 in total)
Late 3 times in a row: the £200 penalties become £1,000 each
Late 3 times in a row and 3 months late: another £1,000 (£2,000 in total)

tax_geared.text: 6 months after the filing deadline (18 months after the end of the accounting period): HMRC estimates the Corporation Tax bill (tax determination) and adds 10% of the unpaid tax
12 months after the filing deadline (24 months after the end of the accounting period): another 10% of any unpaid tax

penalties.older_returns: Returns with a filing date before 1 April 2026 keep the old amounts (£100, £200, £500, £1,000).
penalties.tax_determination: If the return is 6 months late, HMRC writes with the Corporation Tax it thinks is due (a 'tax determination'). It cannot be appealed: the company must file the return and pay the tax due, and HMRC then recalculates interest and penalties.

checks.if: filing_date_due before 2026-04-01 and penalty uses new amounts (or the reverse)
penalty includes 10% or 20% of unpaid tax

checks.note: check whether the earlier two returns really were late

inherits_note: Same reasonable-excuse reasons and routes, read as the company's circumstances (illness or death of the director who files, system failure, fire/flood, HMRC online problems). 'Relied on accountant' and 'didn't know' go to the 'talk first' route.

company_specific_questions.note: If another director could have filed, illness of one director is weaker: route to talk_first

appeal_output.post_to: Corporation Tax Services, HM Revenue and Customs, BX9 1AX
appeal_output.post_to_check: Confirmed on GOV.UK appeal form 9 Nov 2026
